verdict.rationale: Zep documents deletion at all three levels the story asks for. A single memory (fact) can be removed with `client.graph.edge.delete`. Deleting a node deletes the entity and all edges connected to it. Deleting a User removes all Threads and thread artifacts in one API call, which the docs explicitly frame as handling Right To Be Forgotten requests. Missing for 10: explicit confirmation that user deletion also purges the user's Context Graph data and not only threads; independent or hands-on corroboration of the deletion behavior.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can delete a user's memories on demand — single memory, per-entity, or full erasure — to satisfy privacy requirements

citations.quote: Here's how to delete an edge from a graph: client.graph.edge.delete(uuid_="your_edge_uuid")
Deleting a node will also delete all edges connected to that node.
Deleting a User will delete all Threads and thread artifacts associated with that User with a single API call, making it easy to handle Right To Be Forgotten requests.
This single-operation approach makes it simple to handle Right To Be Forgotten (RTBF) requests and comply with privacy regulations.
